title: FZ - 125kHz RFID
html:
FZ - 125kHz RFID

Intro

For background on how 125 kHz tags work, see:

../pentesting-rfid.md

The low-frequency RFID introduction explains the common tag families and their data formats.

Actions

Read

Use Read to capture the tag data. After a successful read, Flipper Zero can emulate the saved tag.[1]

Warning

Some intercom readers attempt to detect writable duplicate tags by issuing a write command before reading. A Flipper Zero emulation does not expose writable tag memory in the same way.[1]

Add manually

You can manually enter tag data in Flipper Zero, save it, and then emulate it.[1]

IDs on cards

Sometimes a card has all or part of its ID printed on its exterior.

  • EM Marin

For example, the pictured EM-Marin card exposes the last three of its five ID bytes. If the tag cannot be read, the two missing bytes may be brute-forced.

  • HID

Similarly, the pictured HID card prints only two of the three ID bytes.

Emulate/Write

After reading a tag or entering its ID manually, Flipper Zero can emulate the saved credential. For supported writable tags, it can also write the saved data to a compatible card.[1]

References

  • [1] Flipper Zero: Diving into RFID Protocols
